chapter_mission: Show what each choice has cost and what each character still gets to keep after Veranthos.
chapter_turn: The book ends its arcs through chosen aftermath instead of forced symmetry.

scene_plan.purpose: At Veraine's containment, let Ben see an enemy who will adapt rather than repent.
On the ridge, let Sera and Torin resolve into presence without speeches.
Kael's departure and the laugh between Ben and Desh should feel plain, human, and final.

relationship_turns.to: permanent question — Veraine in containment is the book's answer to the villainy question: some people are not convertible, only contained. Her equations in the dust are the book's unresolved counterpoint. She will spend years rationalising; she may produce something important. The book does not tell us which
chosen presence — Sera's arc resolved in a hand on his hand on a ridgeline. She is not fixing him. She is with him. The thousand-year wound has produced something like peace, imperfect and earned

freely departed — the ability to leave is the proof the story was different. Kael does not reject the group; he exercises the freedom the book's argument demanded he be offered. His arc resolves as the absence his body makes when he walks away
equals — the laugh is the GAG wound's scar tissue finally forming. Not forgotten; healed enough to produce sound that is not grief

relationship_turns.from: first renewal share taken (Ch 26 s3, per D2)
relationship_turns.to: departing anchor — Ben leaves Veranthos with the tether in his perception. The commitment is priced; the price is that he will return, and the return is no longer a burden but a rhythm. The priced commitment now has shape in the chapter's closing register

exit_vector: Kael's transport lifting from the camp. Sera and Torin small on the ridgeline. Veraine's containment visible in the middle distance with the guard posted. The Steady Returns on the pad, Desh already running pre-flight. Ben at the ramp, the renewal tether (per Ch 26 D2) registered in his perception as a continuous presence — the seal he is leaving but not leaving permanently; the renewal he will return to. The laugh still in the air. One scene left in the book, and it is on Coruscant.
notes: Keep the chapter quiet. Veraine stays unconverted, Sera stays by choice, Kael leaves by choice, and the laugh matters because the book earned it.
